exposure: sociodemographic factors (age, region, race, education, marital status)
maternal and child health indicators (antenatal visits, mode of birth, teenage motherhood, Maternal Mortality Committee activity)
outcome: maternal mortality from direct obstetric causes
maternal mortality from indirect obstetric causes
time of death (during pregnancy or puerperium)
cohort: The study analyzed aggregate data on maternal mortality and live births across Brazil between 2011 and 2021.
finding: The study revealed that sociodemographic factors and maternal and child health indicators were associated with varying patterns of obstetric mortality in Brazil, differing by region, marital status, race, delivery type, prenatal care, and cause of death.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries were associated with a higher indirect specific mortality risk, and certain sociodemographic factors, such as young maternal age and unmarried status, were linked to increased rates of cesarean sections.
